summary.text: Mechanics is the part of physics that studies how force, matter and motion relate to one another among physical objects.
Its basic idea is that forces applied to an object can change its position relative to its surroundings.
Classical mechanics was founded by Galileo, Kepler, Huygens and Newton, and was later challenged by relativistic and quantum mechanics in the 20th century.

facts.label: Name origin
facts.value: From the Ancient Greek word for 'of machines'

facts.label: Newton's landmark
facts.value: The Principia of 1687, built on the new mathematics of calculus

facts.label: Galileo's statement
facts.value: His Two New Sciences of 1638 gave his final account of falling bodies

facts.label: Modern challengers
facts.value: General relativity and quantum mechanics, both from the 20th century

items.prompt: A pushed shopping cart rolls across a parking lot and ends up somewhere new. Which idea from mechanics describes what happened?

options.label: A force acted on the cart and moved it relative to its surroundings
The cart's position changed on its own with no cause at all
Matter and motion are unrelated, so the push was irrelevant
Only machines made of metal can be studied by this branch

items.explain: Mechanics links force, matter and motion: a force on an object can displace it, meaning change its position relative to its environment.

items.prompt: Why is the name of this branch of physics a fitting one?

options.label: It comes from a Greek word meaning 'of the stars'
It comes from a Greek word meaning 'of machines'
It comes from a Greek word meaning 'of heat'
It comes from a Greek word meaning 'of light'

items.explain: The word comes from Ancient Greek meaning 'of machines', a hint at the branch's focus on forces and motion in physical objects.

items.prompt: An engineer wants to describe how a spacecraft moves along its orbit, and a physicist wants to describe a tiny atomic nucleus. Which tools fit?

options.label: Quantum rules for the spacecraft, classical rules for the nucleus
Classical rules for both, since size makes no difference
Classical rules for the spacecraft, quantum rules for the nucleus
Quantum rules for both, since classical ones are obsolete

items.explain: The spacecraft's orbit and rotation are handled by the relativistic theory of classical mechanics, while an atomic nucleus is described by quantum mechanics.

items.prompt: A physicist models a planet as a single mathematical point, ignoring its inner structure. What kind of body is that model treating it as?

options.label: A rigid body with orientation as an extra freedom
A particle, a body with little known internal structure
An elastic body that can stretch and spring back
A fluid body whose parts can flow past each other

items.explain: Classical mechanics treats particles as mathematical points with little known internal structure; rigid bodies add size, shape and orientation.

items.prompt: Medieval scholars like Ibn Sina and Buridan wrote about a thrown stone staying in motion. What problem were they working on?

options.label: How force on a thrown object keeps it going afterward
How machines can be built from simple gears and levers
How the speed of light relates to the size of atoms
How heat moves from a hot object into a cold one

items.explain: Projectile motion was a central problem, and ideas like impetus and inclination tried to explain why a thrown object continues moving.

items.prompt: Someone says Newton invented every idea behind classical mechanics from nothing. What is the more accurate picture?

options.label: Newton's Principia drew on no earlier thinkers at all
Newton only copied Aristotle and added a few new words
Newton wrote nothing about how falling bodies behave
Newton's work was key, but earlier scholars developed many ideas

items.explain: The Principia is the seminal work, yet ideas on inertia and falling bodies had been developed by earlier scholars such as Huygens and medieval predecessors.
